value.title: Three-symbol face bounds for the two-letter Marton functional
value.summary: The proof derives support-line inequalities for the one-letter half-skew BSSC and a two-factor chain identity, reducing every finite two-letter Marton value to a support-sensitive mutual-information functional plus a fixed BSSC term. Product-channel symmetries place the four three-symbol faces into two orbits. Concavity, an exact stationary-point calculation for the endpoint-missing orbit, and a rational tangent certificate for the mixed-missing orbit bound every law supported on at most three super-input symbols strictly below 0.695 bits. Conditioning away any selected symbol and applying the same face bounds yields the quantitative mass floors required of an improving law.

value.title: Rational RTD benchmark and full-support mass-floor certificate
value.summary: Two independent copies of the fair reflected randomized-time-division schedule with conditional priors 1/6 and 5/6 have exact unnormalized value B_{1/6}=2h_2(1/4)+h_2(1/12)-h_2(5/12)-1/3>0.7231 bits. Directed evaluations of the support-sensitive bounds at masses 1/180 and 1/325 separate those thresholds strictly from B_{1/6}, giving required masses greater than 1/180 on 00 and 11 and greater than 1/325 on 01 and 10 for every witness improving on the optimal repeated one-letter RTD benchmark.

value.title: Exact three-symbol-face and mass-floor verifier
value.summary: A Python standard-library verifier constructs the product BSSC transition matrices with exact rational arithmetic, checks the two input and output symmetries and the two face orbits, verifies the affine output laws used in the face calculations, and uses outward-rounded high-precision intervals to check the orbit bounds, rational RTD benchmark, mass-floor thresholds, and all strict separations. These checks corroborate but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.title: Full super-input support is necessary for a two-letter Marton gain
value.summary: For the half-skew BSSC product channel, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input is supported on at most three of 00, 01, 10, and 11 has unnormalized Marton sum value strictly below 0.695 bits. An explicit repeated rational randomized-time-division schedule has exact value B_{1/6}>0.7231 bits. Therefore every strict two-letter Marton improvement over twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value must use all four super-input symbols, with masses greater than 1/180 on each of 00 and 11 and greater than 1/325 on each of 01 and 10. This is a support-pruning theorem, not an unrestricted capacity converse or a full-support no-gain theorem.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted theorem directly advances the active multiletter Marton objective by strengthening super-input support pruning from two-symbol exclusion to quantitative full-support necessity for any two-letter gain.
